authors.bio: Madeleine Noland is the president of the Advanced Television Systems Committee (mnoland@atsc.org). Widely respected for her consensus-building leadership style, she chaired the ATSC Technology Group that oversees the ATSC 3.0 broadcast standard before being named ATSC president in May 2019. Previously, as a representative of LG Electronics, she chaired various ATSC 3.0-related specialist groups, ad hoc groups, and implementation teams since 2012. A 15-year industry veteran, she held key technology management and standards roles with Backchannelmedia Inc., Telvue Corporation, and LG. She received TV NewsCheck ’s “2019 Futurist” Women in Technology Award and was named one of 2018’s “Powerful Women in Consumer Technology” by Dealerscope magazine. In 2016, she received ATSC’s highest technical honor, the Bernard J. Lechner Outstanding Contributor Award. She graduated cum laude from the University of Massachusetts, Amherst, MA.
authors.name: Madeleine Noland

authors.bio: Jerry Whitaker is the vice president for Standards Development, Advanced Television Systems Committee (jwhitaker@atsc.org). He supports the work of the various ATSC technology and specialist groups and assists in the development of ATSC standards and related documents. He currently serves as the secretary of the Technology Group on Next Generation Broadcast Television and is closely involved in work relating to educational programs. He is a Fellow of the Society of Broadcast Engineers, a Life Fellow of SMPTE, and a member of IEEE Broadcast Technology Society (BTS). He has served as a board member and the vice president of the SBE.
authors.name: Jerry Whitaker
